### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The 70-year-old woman presents with unilateral vision loss, sudden and painless onset, which raises suspicion for a vascular event, particularly giant cell arteritis (GCA). GCA can lead to vision loss due to inflammation of the blood vessels, particularly the temporal arteries. The most appropriate initial test to evaluate for vascular involvement in this context is Angio Magnetic Resonance (option c), as it provides detailed imaging of the blood vessels and can help identify any occlusions or inflammatory changes. While C Reactive Protein (option b) can indicate inflammation, it does not provide immediate vascular assessment. Carotid ultrasound (option d) is a non-invasive test that can assess for carotid artery involvement but is less definitive than Angio Magnetic Resonance in this acute setting. Lumbar puncture (option a) is not indicated as the first step in this scenario. Therefore, the best initial test is Angio Magnetic Resonance.
